description: The substrate's foundational theory of grounding, as architectural consequence of Axiom 0 (frame-relativity of truth). Once truth is frame-relative — i.e. only reference is primitive — binary grounding (Concept refers_to {Concept | Unknown}) is incoherent. Grounding becomes a VECTOR in a multi-dimensional space whose dimensions are: frames (Mts), modalities (perceptual / inferential / testimonial / pragmatic / structural), and aspects (coverage, coherence, stability, conviction). Vector grounding enables: simultaneously holding inconsistent views (different components in different Mts), measuring 'how wrong' (vector displacement, not boolean error), partial reference (a name's vector pointing at multiple referents with weights), coherence between concepts (alignment of vectors), conviction (vector magnitude). The substrate's existing machinery already lives in this regime — phonology_divergence Impasses carry Bernoulli-KL vectors; the binary refers_to is the residue, not the rule. This Mt formalises the theory; architecture migration follows. Note: this is NOT a relativist claim that anything goes — vectors live in a structured space with well-defined operations, distances, and compositions; truth is still structural, just structurally-indexed and graded.
category_inheritance: genlMt → compiler_theory + philosophy + mathematics. The vector space of grounding is itself a mathematical structure: each frame contributes an axis (philosophy: axiom 0); each refers_to is a weighted edge (mathematics: linear algebra); inconsistency becomes orthogonality (philosophy: paraconsistency); wrongness becomes distance (compiler_theory: cost equivalence, generalised).

concepts.name: axiom_zero_implies_vector_grounding
concepts.definition: If truth is frame-relative (Axiom 0), then grounding-in-a-frame is graded — a frame is not a partition, it's a dimension. Across multiple frames, grounding becomes a vector.
concepts.why: Inevitable consequence. Once you accept no view from nowhere, binary grounding presupposes one. The substrate's existing binary refers_to is residue of pre-Axiom-0 thinking. Vector is the architecturally consistent form.

concepts.name: grounding_vector_definition
concepts.definition: Concept c has a grounding vector g(c) ∈ R^d where d = sum of frame dimensions + modality dimensions + aspect dimensions. Each component g_i(c) ∈ [0, 1] (or [-1, 1] for signed disagreement).
concepts.why: Formal model. Components per dimension, not per Mt — Mt is one kind of dimension. Modality + aspect are others. d not fixed; grows with frame set.

concepts.name: frame_dimensions
concepts.definition: For each Microtheory Mt_i in the substrate's frame set, g has a component g_{Mt_i}(c) ∈ [0,1] = strength of c's grounding in Mt_i.
concepts.why: Cyc-style ist-formula generalised: not P-in-Mt boolean, but P-in-Mt graded. 'Pain' grounded ~1.0 in folk_psychology, ~0.7 in neuroscience (some C-fiber identity), ~0.3 in chess (metaphorical only).

concepts.name: modality_dimensions
concepts.definition: Orthogonal to frame: perceptual, inferential, testimonial, pragmatic, structural. Each contributes a component.
concepts.why: Different ways a concept can be grounded. 'Red' perceptually grounded (cortex sees it), structurally grounded (in colour-wheel concept), testimonially grounded (others called it red). These compose differently.

concepts.name: aspect_dimensions
concepts.definition: Coverage (how much of the concept's extension is represented), coherence (consistency of representation), stability (resistance to revision), conviction (strength).
concepts.why: Within-frame quality measures. A concept can be coherent + stable but low coverage (well-understood narrow). Or wide coverage + low coherence (broad but contradictory).

concepts.name: binary_grounding_is_residue
concepts.definition: The substrate's existing refers_to → {Concept | Unknown} is binary because vector wasn't available; it's the projection of the vector onto {0, 1} via threshold.
concepts.why: Existing machinery isn't wrong, just compressed. Reads as 'g_{Mt_current}(c) > τ → grounded'. Restoring the vector recovers the lost information. Migration: thresholded readout from full vector for legacy code paths.

concepts.name: phonology_divergence_already_vectoral
concepts.definition: The substrate's phonology_divergence Impasse already carries Bernoulli-KL between observed signature + word template — a divergence (distance in grounding space). Vector grounding is the generalisation.
concepts.why: Foundation already there. Speech recognition produces a divergence vector; substrate compares it to thresholds. Generalising: every Concept reference produces such a vector. Foundation already proven in phonology.

concepts.name: Unknown_as_zero_vector
concepts.definition: An Unknown node corresponds to the zero vector (or near-zero in all components). The substrate uses Unknown to mark 'I don't know what this refers to'. In vector grounding: g(c) ≈ 0.
concepts.why: Unifies. Unknown isn't a separate node type; it's a Concept with zero grounding vector. Holding 'I have no grounding for this' is a vector state, like having grounding is.

concepts.name: ist_formula_as_projection
concepts.definition: Cyc's ist(Mt, P) becomes a projection: ist_grounded(Mt, c) = g_{Mt}(c). Binary ist(Mt, P) recovered as threshold.
concepts.why: Generalisation of Mt-relative truth. ist(physics_Mt, 'water is H2O') = high value in physics dimension. Binary ist recovers via threshold. Same architecture, more information.

concepts.name: wrongness_as_vector_displacement
concepts.definition: How wrong is concept c (held with grounding vector g_held) vs. target g_target? ‖g_held - g_target‖. Distance in grounding space.
concepts.why: Quantifies error. Vector distance = magnitude of correction needed. Direction = which dimensions are off. Far more informative than 'wrong / right'.

concepts.name: how_wrong_per_dimension
concepts.definition: Component-wise: (g_held - g_target)_i tells you, in dimension i, how off. Negative = under-grounded; positive = over-grounded; zero = aligned.
concepts.why: Targeted correction. Substrate can say: 'in dimension perceptual you're under-grounded; in dimension testimonial you're over-grounded'. Vs flat 'wrong'.

concepts.name: conviction_as_magnitude
concepts.definition: ‖g(c)‖ = how strongly grounded the concept is overall. Zero = empty; large = high conviction across many dimensions.
concepts.why: Magnitude separable from direction. A confident wrong belief has high magnitude in wrong direction. A nascent right idea has low magnitude in right direction. Different from each other.

concepts.name: coherence_as_alignment
concepts.definition: Cosine similarity of g(c_1) and g(c_2). Aligned = same components are grounded; orthogonal = independent; antialigned = systematic disagreement.
concepts.why: Cosine vs Euclidean. Direction in grounding space encodes 'which kind of grounding'. Two concepts can be incoherent (anti-aligned vectors) yet both have high magnitude.

concepts.name: multiple_inconsistent_views_simultaneously
concepts.definition: Different Mts may yield different g_{Mt_i}(c) values. The vector holds all simultaneously. No internal pressure to collapse.
concepts.why: Resolves paraconsistency cleanly. 'Heat is caloric (folk)' + 'heat is kinetic energy (physics)' = vector with high in folk_Mt + high in physics_Mt. Substrate holds both; uses appropriate one per query frame.

concepts.name: frame_relativity_not_relativism
concepts.definition: Frames are dimensions of a structured space, not arbitrary perspectives. Vector grounding allows graded truth; doesn't dissolve truth into opinion.
concepts.why: Pre-empts dismissal. Relativism: 'anything is true relative to a frame'. Vector grounding: 'how true depends on frame, measured against structural commitments of that frame'. Substantive constraint.

concepts.name: vector_grounding_extends_substrate_features
concepts.definition: Babbling produces grounding-vector samples (not binary edges). Curiosity drive becomes 'reduce uncertainty in vector' (information gain). Sufficiency emotion becomes 'magnitude > threshold + coherence > threshold'.
concepts.why: Existing substrate machinery extends naturally. Curiosity = expected information gain in vector space. Sufficiency = sufficient magnitude + coherence in target frame. Babble = sample-based estimation of vector.

concepts.name: competent_man_sufficiency_thresholded_magnitude
concepts.definition: The 'yeah yeah the time knife, we've all seen it' sufficiency emotion = magnitude in target frame exceeds threshold τ_competent. Move on.
concepts.why: Threshold over vector magnitude. Different per frame: chess Mt needs high magnitude for piece-rules; quantum Mt's competent threshold lower (nobody fully grounds). Existing mechanism in substrate, now formalised.

concepts.name: babble_extends_to_vector_sampling
concepts.definition: Babble (form + test across boundary) produces grounding-vector estimates. Each cycle samples; estimates converge to true vector.
concepts.why: Existing babble loop generalises. Currently binary: word produced, recognised yes/no. Vector: word produced, recognition vector returned (per-Mt). Substrate's grounding mechanism + vector grounding align.

concepts.name: embedding_spaces_partial_vector_grounding
concepts.definition: Modern ML embeddings (Word2Vec, BERT, CLIP) are partial vector groundings — single-frame (training distribution), single-modality (the loss). Vector grounding generalises to multi-frame, multi-modality.
concepts.why: ML's embeddings are a vector-grounding intuition pump but limited: one frame, one loss. Substrate's vector grounding extends to many frames + modalities. Relates substrate to ML positively.

concepts.name: Dempster_Shafer_evidence_partial_match
concepts.definition: Dempster-Shafer assigns mass to subsets of hypotheses; combines via Dempster's rule. Partial overlap with vector grounding (mass per subset vs degree per dimension).
concepts.why: Existing mathematical framework. Vector grounding has more structure (dimensions, not subsets) but DS provides composition operations. Useful precedent.

concepts.name: fuzzy_logic_per_dimension_partial
concepts.definition: Fuzzy logic: graded membership in single category. Vector grounding: graded grounding in multiple dimensions simultaneously. Strict generalisation.
concepts.why: Fuzzy partial; vector full. Fuzzy: 'x is somewhat tall'. Vector: 'x is somewhat tall in folk Mt + structurally tall in measurement Mt + tested-tall in testimonial Mt'.

concepts.name: paraconsistent_logic_alignment
concepts.definition: Paraconsistent logic: contradictions don't trivialise. Vector grounding: contradictions are orthogonal components, both held with positive magnitude.
concepts.why: Different mechanism for same goal. Paraconsistent: weaker entailment. Vector: same entailment, distinct dimensions. Substrate's preferred mechanism.

concepts.name: Concept_grounding_vector_attr
concepts.definition: Architecturally: each Concept node gains attribute `grounding_vector: Map<Dimension, float>`. Dimensions include Mt names + modality enum + aspect enum.
concepts.why: Concrete graph schema. Backwards compatible: legacy binary refers_to maps to threshold over Mt-dimension component. New code can read the full vector.

concepts.name: refers_to_edge_becomes_weighted
concepts.definition: Architecturally: refers_to edge gains weight vector. Binary 'A refers_to B' becomes 'A refers_to B with vector w' (single edge can carry multi-component weight).
concepts.why: Concrete graph schema. Phonology divergence already does this with Bernoulli-KL; generalising. Substrate's typed graph already supports edge attrs.

concepts.name: Unknown_node_collapses_to_zero_vector_Concept
concepts.definition: Architecturally: Unknown becomes a Concept with grounding_vector = 0. Or eliminated entirely (no node, just empty vector).
concepts.why: Schema simplification. Either treatment works. Empty vector is the meaning of 'I don't know what this is'.

concepts.name: Impasse_vector_valued
concepts.definition: Architecturally: Impasse nodes (currently scalar threshold breach) become vector-valued — they record the specific vector displacement (which dimensions, how much) that triggered them.
concepts.why: Concrete graph schema. phonology_divergence already shape-vector-compatible; other Impasses (predicate_churn, hypothesis_dryness) extend similarly. Diagnostics improve.

concepts.name: operations_on_grounding_vectors
concepts.definition: Operations: composition (chain grounding), aggregation (average over Mts), projection (read one dimension), distance (wrongness), similarity (coherence), magnitude (conviction).
concepts.why: Mathematical operations needed for architecture. Each maps to standard linear algebra. No exotic math required.

concepts.name: migration_strategy_thresholded_readout
concepts.definition: Existing code reading binary refers_to gets thresholded view: g_{Mt_current}(c) > τ → 'grounded'. New code reads full vector.
concepts.why: Backwards compatibility. Substrate has many Mts already using binary; can't migrate atomically. Compatibility layer. Phonology already vector — its readout is the model.

concepts.name: axiom_zero_no_view_from_nowhere
concepts.definition: Axiom 0 from philosophy Mt. Restated here as foundation: no privileged frame. Reference is primitive; truth is frame-relative.
concepts.why: Foundation of vector grounding. Already in philosophy Mt; here as the load-bearing premise. Vector grounding is its architectural form.

concepts.name: structural_constraint_not_anything_goes
concepts.definition: Vectors live in structured space. Mt dimensions have internal commitments (admissibility constraints). Grounding-in-Mt means satisfying those commitments, gradedly.
concepts.why: Resists 'relativism eats truth'. Each Mt's dimension is constrained by its admissibility grammar. High grounding in Mt = high alignment with that Mt's structural commitments. Substantive.

rules.name: Axiom_zero_entails_graded_grounding
then: grounding in a frame is graded; across frames it is a vector
rules.why: If no frame is privileged, then 'is this grounded?' has no frame-independent answer. Best you can do is 'how grounded in each available frame?'. That answer is a vector. Inevitable consequence.

rules.name: binary_grounding_loses_information
then: per-frame strength + coherence + multiple-view information lost
rules.why: Boolean is a projection of vector onto {0, 1}. Information-destructive. Substrate has been doing this everywhere except phonology. Migration recovers the information.

rules.name: vector_distance_is_wrongness
if: concept held with vector g_held vs target g_target
rules.why: Distance in grounding space. Vector form not only says wrong, but how wrong (magnitude) and which dimensions are off (direction). Foundation of useful self-correction.

rules.name: multiple_views_coexist_without_collapse
if: concept has different grounding in Mt_a and Mt_b
then: vector holds both simultaneously; no forced consistency
rules.why: Inconsistent views in different Mts → different components of vector. Paraconsistent by construction. Substrate uses the Mt-appropriate component per query, doesn't collapse globally.

rules.name: coherence_distinct_from_grounding
if: two concepts have grounding vectors g_1, g_2
then: coherence between them = cosine(g_1, g_2), distinct from individual groundings
rules.why: Coherence = directional alignment. Two well-grounded but anti-aligned concepts = high magnitude, low coherence. Different quality measures. Foundation of detecting internal contradiction.

rules.name: sufficiency_threshold_per_frame
if: frame Mt_i has competent threshold τ_i
rules.why: Competent-man sufficiency formalised. Each frame has its own threshold for 'enough'. Substrate moves on when threshold met in target frame. 'Yeah yeah the time knife' is τ_competent met.

rules.name: babble_samples_grounding_vector
if: babble cycle produces form + test across cortex boundary
then: one sample of grounding vector at that point
rules.why: Many cycles → estimate of true vector. Existing babble loop reframes: not binary success/fail, but vector sample. Substrate's grounding mechanism formalised.

rules.name: frame_relativity_is_not_relativism
if: frame_relative grounding + structural constraints per Mt
then: truth is graded + indexed but not arbitrary
rules.why: Pre-empt dismissal. Vector lives in structured space. Each Mt-dimension constrained by admissibility grammar. High grounding = alignment with structure. Substantive. Defends Axiom 0 against straw-man relativism.

rules.name: phonology_divergence_template_for_other_Mts
if: substrate already has vector-valued Impasses in phonology
then: other Mts can adopt same pattern
rules.why: Foundation already proven in production. phonology_divergence carries Bernoulli-KL vector; recognition uses thresholds + direction. Other Mts (chess, physics, language) adopt same pattern. Architecture proven.

rules.name: Concept_attr_extension_backwards_compatible
then: legacy binary refers_to readers see thresholded projection
rules.why: Migration path. Concept gets optional vector attr; legacy code that reads refers_to → {C | U} sees threshold-based view. Vector-aware code reads full vector. Atomic migration unnecessary.

rules.name: Impasse_carries_displacement_vector
then: it records displacement vector that caused it
rules.why: Diagnostics improvement. Currently: 'predicate churn impasse fired'. With vector: 'churn in dimensions {coverage, coherence} by amount d'. Targeted response possible. Aligned with substrate's existing meta-monitor work.

rules.name: vector_grounding_is_substrate_design_position
then: vector grounding is the architecturally consistent form
rules.why: Foundation. Binary grounding presupposes a privileged frame; substrate denies privileged frame. Vector grounding follows. The substrate's existing binary edges are residue to migrate, not features to preserve.
